0.headline: IPO-bound Anarock’s FY26 operating cash flow turns negative despite 53% rise in profit
0.heading: IPO-bound Anarock’s FY26 operating cash flow turns negative despite 53% rise in profit
0.intro: Anarock acquired 53.68% of DSP Design for Rs 64.01 crore just three days before filing its IPO papers. Of the proposed Rs 1,000-crore issue, Rs 550 crore will go to the company and Rs 450 crore to selling shareholders
0.body:
IPO-bound Anarock Property Consultants reported a 53 percent rise in net profit in FY26 even as cash flow from its operations turned negative ahead of its proposed Rs 1,000-crore initial public offering.

The Anuj Puri-led property consultancy reported a net profit of Rs 93.22 crore in FY26, up from Rs 60.78 crore a year earlier, according to the company’s draft red herring prospectus (DRHP). Revenue rose 34 percent to Rs 881.90 crore from Rs 658.95 crore.

Operating cash flow, however, swung to an outflow of Rs 12.07 crore in FY26 from an inflow of about Rs 93 crore in FY25, the DRHP showed.

The decline in cash generation came as trade receivables — money owed to Anarock by customers — increased to Rs 464.21 crore at the end of FY26 from Rs 316 crore a year earlier.

The cash-flow numbers come as Anarock prepares to tap the public markets and expands its business through acquisitions.

Anarock acquired 53.68 percent of DSP Design Associates for Rs 64.01 crore on September 27, 2026, through a combination of fresh investment and purchases from existing shareholders, according to the DRHP. Three days later, it filed its papers for the proposed IPO.

DSP also reported negative operating cash flow in FY26. Its operating cash outflow stood at Rs 1.61 crore, compared with an inflow of Rs 11.95 crore in FY25, according to financial information disclosed in the DRHP.

The acquisition therefore brings together two businesses that reported negative operating cash flows in FY26.

Anarock was launched by Anuj Puri in 2017 after he left JLL India, where he had served as chairman and country head. The company began with a focus on residential property advisory and has since expanded into transaction advisory, commercial leasing, investment advisory, project management and engineering, and technology-based real estate services. Its businesses also cover retail, hospitality, industrial and logistics, land, investment banking and valuations.

As of March 31, 2026, Anarock had 2,192 permanent employees and operated across 15 cities in India, along with operations in the Middle East, according to the DRHP.

Profit rises, cash flow turns negative

Anarock’s revenue from operations increased 33.83 percent to Rs 881.90 crore in FY26 from Rs 658.95 crore in FY25, while profit after tax rose 53.38 percent to Rs 93.22 crore from Rs 60.78 crore, according to the DRHP.

The company’s revenue from operations stood at Rs 509.23 crore in FY24, while net profit was Rs 44.94 crore.

The increase in reported earnings in FY26, however, was accompanied by a deterioration in operating cash flow.

Trade receivables increased by about Rs 148 crore during the year to Rs 464.21 crore. Trade receivables are amounts owed by customers for services for which revenue has already been recognised but payment has yet to be received.

Anarock attributed the increase partly to growth in revenue and the timing of revenue recognition and billing. Revenue recognised towards the end of the financial year leaves less time for the corresponding payments to be collected before March 31, the company said in its DRHP.

The increase in receivables does not by itself indicate collection problems. However, experts told Moneycontrol that the sharp deterioration in operating cash flow, despite higher profits, makes Anarock’s ability to convert its earnings into cash an important metric to watch ahead of the IPO.

Anarock’s transaction advisory business, which primarily includes residential property sales, generated Rs 442.45 crore in revenue in FY26, according to the DRHP.

Leasing and investment advisory, including commercial leasing, investment banking and hospitality advisory, contributed Rs 306.83 crore, while management services, including project management and engineering, generated Rs 89.17 crore.

DSP adds revenue faster than profit

The DSP acquisition significantly increases Anarock’s revenue base, but its contribution to profit is proportionately smaller, according to proforma financial information disclosed in the DRHP.

Since the acquisition took place after FY26, DSP is not included in Anarock’s reported financial results for the year. The company has provided proforma figures showing what its FY26 financials would have looked like had DSP been part of the group for the full year.

On that basis, revenue would have been Rs 1,123.87 crore, about 27 percent higher than Anarock’s reported Rs 881.90 crore.

Net profit, however, would have been Rs 100.07 crore, only about 7 percent higher than the reported Rs 93.22 crore.

The combined net profit margin would have been 8.90 percent, compared with Anarock’s reported margin of 10.57 percent.

DSP generated revenue of Rs 241.97 crore in FY26 and net profit of Rs 6.86 crore, translating into a net profit margin of 2.83 percent, according to the DRHP.

Incorporated in 1999, DSP provides architecture, interior design, corporate office fit-outs, design-and-build and project management services.

Anarock said in the DRHP that the acquisition will strengthen its project management and engineering services business, add longer-duration revenue streams and allow it to offer corporate clients services ranging from leasing and design to office execution.

Anarock proposes to use Rs 148 crore of the fresh issue proceeds to acquire additional shares in DSP.

The company has also earmarked Rs 120 crore for technology and artificial intelligence across its businesses and Rs 89.5 crore to strengthen existing businesses and add specialised services through hiring. The remaining proceeds from the fresh issue are proposed to be used for acquisitions, other strategic initiatives and general corporate purposes, according to the DRHP.

The proposed Rs 1,000-crore IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 550 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 450 crore. The proceeds from the offer-for-sale portion will go to the selling shareholders and not to Anarock.

A spokesperson for Anarock declined to comment citing silent period following the DRHP filing.

1.headline: Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO fully subscribed on Day 3; NII, retail investors lead demand
1.heading: Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPO fully subscribed on Day 3; NII, retail investors lead demand
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Nityas Gems and Jewellery Limited witnessed a modest demand on the final day of bidding, with the issue receiving 1.08 times subscription, as of 11:00 am on October 5, as per NSE data.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Nityas Gems and Jewellery Limited witnessed a modest demand on the final day of bidding, with the issue receiving 1.08 times subscription, as of 11:00 am on October 5, as per NSE data.

The Rs 108.42-crore IPO received bids for 1,56,11,600 shares against 1,44,56,000 shares on offer. Retail investors led the demand, with their portion subscribed 1,56,11,600 times, while the non-institutional investors (NII) category was subscribed 1.02 times.

In the grey market, Nityas Gems and Jewellery shares were trading at a premium of nearly 3 percent on the morning of October 5, according to InvestorGain.

Read Also: Vishal Nirmiti IPO booked 85% so far on Day 3; check latest GMP

Grey market premiums are unofficial indicators of market sentiment and do not guarantee the actual listing price.

The company has fixed the IPO price band at Rs 70-75 per share. The public issue will remain open until October 5. The IPO comprises an entirely fresh issue of 1.44 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component.

At the upper price band of Rs 75 per share, the company aims to raise Rs 108.42 crore through the issue.

The anchor book opened on September 29, a day ahead of the public subscription.

The IPO allotment is likely to be finalised on October 6, while trading in the company's equity shares is expected to commence on the bourses on October 8.

Check IPO News Here

Nityas Gems and Jewellery plans to utilise Rs 70 crore of the net IPO proceeds towards its working capital requirements. The remaining amount will be used for general corporate purposes.

The Gujarat-based company manufactures diamond-studded gold jewellery and operates primarily under a business-to-business (B2B) model, manufacturing jewellery products for retailers and wholesalers.

The company also has a direct-to-consumer (D2C) business through its subsidiary, Ayaani Diamonds and Jewellery, which operates an omnichannel retail business.

2.headline: Vishal Nirmiti IPO: Issue fully subscribed on final day of bidding; check latest GMP
2.heading: Vishal Nirmiti IPO: Issue fully subscribed on final day of bidding; check latest GMP
2.intro: The initial public offering of Vishal Nirmiti witnessed a pick-up in investor interest on the last day of bidding, with the Rs 178-crore public issue receiving 1.05 times subscription as of 10:30 am on October 5, according to NSE data.
2.body:
The initial public offering of Vishal Nirmiti witnessed a pick-up in investor interest on the last day of bidding, with the Rs 178-crore public issue receiving 1.05 times subscription as of 10:30 am on October 5, according to NSE data.

The IPO has received bids for 88,54,756 shares against the 84,71,153 shares on offer. The non-institutional investor category was subscribed 1.18 times, while the retail investor portion was subscribed 99 percent.

The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 145 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 33 crore. The company has fixed the IPO price band at Rs 208-220 per share.

Read Also: Runwal Enterprises shares make flat debut, list at issue price on NSE — should you buy, sell or hold?

The grey market premium (GMP) for the Vishal Nirmiti IPO stood at Rs 20, or around 9 percent, over the upper end of the IPO price band on the morning of October 5, as per InvestorGain.

Grey market premiums are unofficial indicators and can change depending on market conditions and investor sentiment. They should not be considered a reliable indicator of the actual listing price or future performance of the shares.

The Vishal Nirmiti IPO is a book-built issue comprising a fresh issue of 65.91 lakh shares aggregating to Rs 145 crore and an OFS of 15 lakh shares worth Rs 33 crore.

The IPO will close on October 5, while the basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on October 6. The shares are proposed to list on both the NSE and BSE, with October 8 as the tentative listing date.

The lot size is 68 shares, meaning retail investors will need to invest a minimum of Rs 14,960 at the upper end of the price band.

Saffron Capital Advisors Pvt Ltd is the book-running lead manager, while MUFG Intime India Pvt Ltd is the registrar to the issue.

The company plans to use the net proceeds from the fresh issue to fund working capital requirements, repay or pre-pay term loans and meet general corporate purposes.

Of the Rs 94 crore in net proceeds, Rs 75 crore has been earmarked for working capital requirements, while Rs 19 crore will be used for repayment or pre-payment of term loans.

Check IPO News Here

Vishal Nirmiti reported a 6 percent increase in total income to Rs 344 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 325 crore in FY25. Its profit after tax (PAT) also rose 6 percent year-on-year to Rs 25 crore in FY26 from Rs 24 crore in FY25.

About Vishal Nirmiti

Incorporated in 1994, Vishal Nirmiti Ltd, formerly known as Sejal Farms Private Ltd, is engaged in civil engineering, manufacturing and construction activities. The company manufactures and deals in pre-stressed concrete (PSC) sleepers for railways, pre-cast and pre-stressed concrete products, as well as mild steel (MS) pipes, liners and penstock pipes used in pumped storage projects.

It also provides engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) services for railway infrastructure, irrigation and civil engineering projects across railways, renewable power and industrial infrastructure.

Vishal Nirmiti has a pan-India presence, with operational units across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and Karnataka.
